_comment: Canonical msgpack wire contract for the 6 distinct valid CreateIndex shapes (F-81 #908). Built via CreateIndex::try_build().unwrap() and serialized with rmp_serde::to_vec_named (named-field maps). Consumed by the Rust regression test (tests/create_index_try_build_msgpack.rs).
_key_order_note: rmp_serde::to_vec_named emits map keys in Rust STRUCT DECLARATION order: create_index, table, fields, unique, sorted, repo, then optional fields (index_type, fts_*, functional_*, vector_*, include, if_not_exists) in declaration order. skip_serializing_if means: unique=false and sorted=false are emitted as msgpack false (0xc2) because the serde attribute is #[serde(default)] (NOT skip_serializing_if=is_false); Option::is_none fields are absent; Vec::is_empty fields (include, functional_args) are absent. if_not_exists=false is skipped (skip_serializing_if=is_false).

_value_notes.discriminator: BatchOp::CreateIndex(CreateIndexOp) serializes as a single-key map {"create_index": {...fields...}} — the first struct field create_index: String is the BatchOp discriminator key, and its value is the index name string.
_value_notes.bool_defaults: unique=false → 0xc2 (msgpack false), NOT absent. This is because CreateIndexOp uses #[serde(default)] for the bool fields, which means serde writes the default value (false) as msgpack false. Only if_not_exists uses skip_serializing_if=is_false.
_value_notes.vector_dim_384: cd0180 = uint16 384 (0x0180). Values 128-65535 use uint16 (0xcd prefix).
_value_notes.repo_default: repo defaults to 'main' and is always present (#[serde(default = "default_repo")], no skip_serializing_if).
